summary: The discussion proposes implementing QMUX as a multiplexing layer between mock applications and the TCP/TLS stack to enable bidirectional control streams and unidirectional data streams, allowing existing Quick-based code to function across both UDP-friendly and non-UDP environments. While this approach offers compatibility benefits, it introduces trade-offs such as increased round-trip times (RTTs), loss of connection migration features, and potential head-of-line blocking. The conversation concludes by addressing identification mechanisms via ALPN and exploring strategies to minimize connection setup latency when negotiating QMUX support.
